subject: VPC data control: erasure requests, attestation, and log proof
messages:

Subject: Questions on private VPC erasure process and attestation

Hi Soojin / Rishi,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Before we proceed with a pilot, our compliance team needs clarification on a few items related to the Private (VPC) deployment:

- How is customer data erased when requested? What are the steps (application layer, storage, snapshots, backups)?
- Can you provide a verifiable attestation (signed) that data was removed for a given tenant? What does that proof look like?
- How long do backups/snapshots persist by default in the Private offering and can that be changed?
- Which logs can you provide to demonstrate deletion activity (access logs, object deletion events, timestamps)?
- If keys are customer-managed (KMS/HSM), what extra confirmation do you need from our side?

We’re evaluating Redwood for a regulated analytics workload; these answers will go into our security questionnaire. I attached a small data map for context.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-analytics.com>, Evan Soto <evan.soto@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on private VPC erasure process and attestation

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I’ve attached our Private VPC erasure playbook and a small sample audit extract. We can follow up with a technical call to walk the runbook if helpful.

1) Data deletion flow (Private/VPC):
   - Control-plane request: Customer (via API or Console) triggers a tenant data erasure. In Private deployments the control plane can be customer-hosted or redwood-managed depending on the contract; we honor the trigger either way.
   - Application-layer: Application metadata and indexes are immediately marked for deletion (soft-delete).
   - KV cache / inference caches: KV caches and in-memory caches for the tenant are evicted immediately; we issue asynchronous requests to all serving nodes to flush related keys.
   - Storage layer: Objects are marked deleted and garbage-collected according to the configured storage backend. For cloud-backed setups we issue delete APIs to object storage; for on-prem we execute the equivalent purge procedures in coordination with customer infra.
   - Snapshots & backups: By default snapshots are retained for 30 days in the Private plan (configurable in the provisioning template). Backups are scheduled and have a separate retention policy; they are removed according to the configured retention window and a background sweep removes references to deleted tenant data.

2) Attestation and proof:
   - We can provide a signed deletion attestation that includes: list of object identifiers deleted, deletion timestamps (ISO8601), storage backend confirmation IDs (where available), and a SHA-256 digest over the ordered list. The attestation is signed by Redwood’s code-signing key (or by a vendor-managed HSM if applicable).
   - For customer-managed KMS, the attestation will reference the key IDs and we can provide logs showing that key material was not used post-deletion.

3) Logs and evidence:
   - We can export object-storage deletion events, control-plane API audit logs, and serving-node eviction logs. These are delivered as CSV/JSON extracts and can be correlated by timestamps.

4) Timelines & soft vs irreversible deletion:
   - Soft-delete is immediate; irreversible removal from the primary storage backend typically completes within 24–72 hours, depending on snapshot/backfill windows and backend GC cycles.
   - Snapshot/backups can extend visibility to up to the configured retention window; for accelerated erasure we offer a paid expedited workflow to purge snapshots within 48 hours (requires coordination).

Next steps: I’ve attached the runbook (redwood-vpc-erasure-playbook.pdf) and a sample audit extract (sample-audit-report.csv). Rishi can add implementation details about signed attestations and the API endpoints to call. Would you like to schedule a 30-min technical call tomorrow or Wednesday?

Tx,
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Trust (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-vpc-erasure-playbook.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on private VPC erasure process and attestation

Hi Laura — adding a technical addendum with example APIs, artifacts we can produce, and notes on cryptographic attestation.

API examples (Private control plane):
- Trigger erasure: POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/actions/erase  (payload: {"scope":"all","request_id":"<uuid>"})
- Check status: GET /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/actions/{request_id}/status
- Export audit bundle: GET /api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/audit?from=2026-04-01&to=2026-04-30

Artifacts we can provide after an erasure request:
- control_plane_audit.csv (entries for the erase request with timestamps and actor)
- storage_deletes.csv (object ids + delete timestamp + backend-confirmation-id)
- serving_evictions.log (node-level eviction messages)
- signed_attestation.txt (JSON blob containing deletion manifest + SHA256 digest + Redwood signature)

Cryptographic attestation notes: we produce a deletion manifest M = [o1, o2, o3...], ordered by object id. We compute D = SHA256(M) and produce a signed statement:
  {"tenant_id":"...","request_id":"...","manifest_digest":"<hex>","deleted_at":"2026-04-20T10:20:12Z","signer":"redwood-root"}
This is signed using Redwood’s PKI (or HSM-backed key where configured). You can verify the signature against our published public key.

Edge cases / KMS:
- If you bring your own KMS and rotate or destroy customer keys, we will require a key reference and a proof-of-destruction (if keys are destroyed) to fully attest that ciphertext cannot be decrypted. If keys are customer-managed and you request erasure, we coordinate to verify the key state in the KMS audit logs.

Retention tuning: in Private deployments our provisioning template exposes snapshot_retention_days and backup_window parameters. We can set snapshot_retention_days=0 for aggressive delete policies (note: may impact point-in-time restore guarantees).

Sample signed attestation (placeholder header):
-----BEGIN SIGNED-ATTESTATION-----
redwood-attest-v1; tenant: ACME-12345; request: 9f8a-...; digest: ef34a3...; deleted_at: 2026-04-20T10:20:12Z
(signature blob omitted)
-----END SIGNED-ATTESTATION-----

Operational note: for expedited snapshot purges and certified attestation we recommend a short SOW so we can coordinate storage admin access windows with your infra team.

Happy to walk through the API and a sample attestation in the technical call.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
